entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Intef II was the third ruler of the Eleventh Dynasty of Egypt during the First Intermediate Period. He reigned for almost fifty years from 2112 BC to 2063 BC. His capital was located at Thebes. In his time, Egypt was split between several local dynasties. He was buried in a saff tomb at El-Tarif.

Intef II played a crucial role in the early stages of the First Intermediate Period, a time marked by political instability and fragmentation. The Eleventh Dynasty, to which he belonged, was one of the several dynasties that emerged during this period. Intef II's reign was characterized by a series of conflicts with neighboring regions, including Nubia and the Near East.

Despite the challenges he faced, Intef II managed to maintain a degree of stability in Egypt, albeit short-lived. His legacy would eventually be overshadowed by the rise of the Twelfth Dynasty, which would go on to shape the course of ancient Egyptian history.

One of the most enduring legacies of Intef II is the continued presence of the Eleventh Dynasty in the Egyptian pantheon of rulers. His name remains an important part of Egypt's rich historical narrative, a testament to the enduring power of its ancient dynasties.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Intef II played a significant role in the early stages of the First Intermediate Period, a time marked by political instability and fragmentation. His reign helped to establish Thebes as a major center of power and culture, cementing its position as the capital of Egypt.
